qt: to the Commission Özlem Demirel (The Left) Subject:

On 6 August 2026, the first phase of an EU-funded project to secure the western border began in Libya. It involves the installation of an optical and thermal surveillance system along a section of approximately 200 kilometres in the Al-Assah border sector on the border with Tunisia. The project is being carried out in cooperation with the European Union Integrated Border Management Assistance Mission in Libya (EUBAM Libya). It supports Libyan authorities, amongst other places, at the Ras Ajdir border crossing, in the Al-Assah operational area and at the Abu Sharaf watchtower by providing photovoltaic systems and surveillance technology. 1.

Which organisations or companies were selected as contractors for the supply and installation of the optical and thermal surveillance systems as part of the first phase of the project, and what procedure was followed for the award of the contract?
What are the specific technical components of the system in place – in particular, the type and range of the watchtowers and sensors – and who are the manufacturers?
Other than the technical equipment, what other services are being funded as part of the project, and what are the total costs involved?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.10.2026) The project in question is part of the mandate of EU Border Assistance Mission (EUBAM) Libya as agreed by Member States. On 15 January 2026, in line with the Commission’s regulations, EUBAM Libya selected the local company East Rock as contractor for the supply and installation of the optical and thermal surveillance system. In the market research, eight companies were contacted, and six of them expressed interest. In the final selection, the contract was awarded through negotiated procedure because only one contractor was able to meet all the technical specifications and in possess of all the necessary security clearances. The contract includes ten days of training on usage and maintenance for Libyan officials from the border authorities (it was delivered from 12 to 20 July 2026), and remote assistance, valid from 20 July to 19 December 2026. The total costs are EUR 380 0001.
